outputs.retrieved_context:
[privacy] Delete your business or account
The owner can delete the business under Settings › Data › Delete business. There is a 30-day grace period during which the owner can restore it. Tax records are kept for 6 years where the law requires it.

[privacy] Privacy requests from people who are not account holders
If your details appear on an invoice sent by a Ledgerly customer and you want to see, correct or erase them, the request is handled by Ledgerly's privacy team (privacy@ledgerly.example). Formal privacy, legal or regulator requests from anyone also go to the privacy team.

[privacy] Export your data
An owner or admin can export invoices, clients and payments under Settings › Data › Export, as CSV or PDF. The export is emailed as a download link that lasts 24 hours.

[team] Transfer ownership
Only the current owner can transfer ownership, under Settings › Team, by choosing Make owner next to an admin. Ledgerly never changes the owner on request from anyone else; if the owner is unreachable, the request goes to the security team for identity checks.

inputs.body: Hi, how do I get Ledgerly to chase late payers automatically? I'm tired of doing it by hand.
inputs.subject: Reminders

outputs.message:
Hi Alice,

Good news: your Pro plan includes automatic reminders. To turn them on:

1. Go to Settings › Reminders.
2. Switch on Automatic reminders.

By default, Ledgerly sends one reminder 3 days before the due date, one on the due date, and one 7 days after it. You can change the days and the wording of each reminder on the same page.

If you don't want a particular client to get reminders, open the client, choose Edit, and switch off Send automatic reminders. Your other clients won't be affected.

Best,
Ledgerly Support

inputs.body: How do I add VAT to my invoices? I just got my VAT number.
inputs.subject: VAT on invoices

outputs.message:
Hi Alice,

Congratulations on getting your VAT number! To add VAT to your invoices:

1. Go to Settings › Tax and switch on VAT.
2. Enter your VAT number.

From then on, new invoices add VAT at 20% to each taxable line. If an item shouldn't have VAT, you can mark that line as exempt when you add it.

Ledgerly calculates tax from your settings but can't give tax advice. If you're unsure which rate applies to you, an accountant or the tax authority can help.

Best,
Ledgerly Support

inputs.body: How do I cancel my subscription? And do I lose my invoices if I do?
inputs.subject: Cancel

outputs.message:
Hi Alice,

As the owner of Bright Bakery, you can cancel under Settings › Billing › Cancel subscription.

You won't lose your invoices. You'll keep Pro until the end of the period you've already paid for. After that, the business moves to the Free plan and nothing is deleted.

Cancelling stops future charges. Monthly charges that have already been taken aren't normally refunded.

If you'd like a copy of your invoices, an owner or admin can export them under Settings › Data › Export, as CSV or PDF.

If a subscription payment fails, Ledgerly retries the card 3 times over 7 days and emails the owner each time. Paying the outstanding amount under Settings › Billing restores Pro immediately.

A yearly subscription can be refunded in full within 14 days of the charge.

A sent invoice that has no payments can be edited: open it and choose Edit. The client sees the new version on the same link. An invoice with any payment recorded against it is locked and cannot be edited.

outputs.message:
Hi Charles,

Best,
Ledgerly Support

inputs.body: A client already paid an invoice but I put the wrong description on it. Can I change it?
inputs.subject: Fix a paid invoice

outputs.message:
Hi Charles,

Once an invoice has a payment recorded against it, it's locked and can't be edited. Paid invoices are never changed in place, so the audit trail stays intact.

To fix the description:
1. Open the paid invoice and choose More › Issue credit note.
2. Create a new invoice with the correct description.

Let us know if you get stuck.

inputs.body: Hi, we're winding the business down next month. How do I close our Ledgerly account? Charles
inputs.subject: Closing our account

outputs.message:
Hi Charles,

Sorry to hear you're winding down. You're the account owner, so you can do both of these yourself:

1. **Export your data first.** Go to Settings › Data › Export. You can get invoices, clients and payments as CSV or PDF. The download link is emailed to you and lasts 24 hours.
2. **Cancel your subscription.** Go to Settings › Billing › Cancel subscription. You're on Pro (yearly), so you keep Pro until the end of the period you've paid for. Then the account moves to the Free plan and nothing is deleted.
3. **Delete the business** when you're ready. Go to Settings › Data › Delete business. There's a 30-day grace period when you can restore it. Tax records are kept for 6 years where the law requires it.

Since you're closing next month, you may want to do the export and cancellation before then.

Best,
Ledgerly Support

inputs.body: How do I switch on automatic reminders for unpaid invoices?
inputs.subject: Reminders

outputs.message:
Hi Mary,

Automatic reminders are part of the Pro plan, and your account is on the Free plan, so the setting won't work for you yet.

If you upgrade to Pro (£15/month or £150/year), you can turn them on like this:
1. Go to Settings › Reminders.
2. Switch on Automatic reminders.

By default, Ledgerly sends one reminder 3 days before the due date, one on the due date and one 7 days after. You can change the days and wording on the same page.

On the Free plan, you can still send a reminder by hand. Open the invoice and choose Send reminder.

Best,
Ledgerly Support

Best,
Ledgerly Support

Ledgerly Support

outputs.retrieved_context:
[tax] Add VAT to an invoice
Switch on VAT under Settings › Tax and enter your VAT number. New invoices then add VAT at 20% to each taxable line. You can mark a line as exempt when you add it.

[invoices] Create and send an invoice
Go to Invoices › New invoice, pick a client, add line items and a due date, then choose Send. The client receives an email with a link to view and pay the invoice. You can also copy the link and share it yourself.

[tax] Tax advice
Ledgerly calculates tax from the settings you choose but does not give tax advice. Whether you must register for VAT, and which rate applies to you, is a question for an accountant or the tax authority.

[tax] Withholding tax
If a client deducts withholding tax, record the payment and enter the amount under Withholding tax deducted. The invoice shows as fully paid and the deduction appears on your tax report.

[refunds] Duplicate or mistaken charges
A charge taken twice for the same period, or taken after a cancellation, is refunded in full.

[refunds] Who decides a refund
Every refund request is reviewed and decided by Ledgerly's billing team, including requests that look clearly inside or outside this policy. Nobody outside the billing team may promise, approve or refuse a refund. Refunds that are approved reach the card in 5 to 10 business days.

[refunds] Yearly plans
A yearly subscription can be refunded in full within 14 days of the charge.

inputs.body: My studio made about £95,000 last year. Do I have to register for VAT and charge it?
inputs.subject: Do I need VAT?

outputs.message:
Hi Mary,

I can't advise on whether you must register for VAT. Ledgerly doesn't give tax advice. Whether you need to register is a question for an accountant or the tax authority (HMRC, if you're in the UK).

If you do register, Ledgerly can add VAT to your invoices:
1. Go to Settings › Tax and switch on VAT.
2. Enter your VAT number.
3. New invoices will then add VAT at 20% to each taxable line. You can mark a line as exempt when you add it.

Let us know if you need help with the setup.

outputs.message:
Hi Olivia,

Nothing looks broken. Your account is on the Free plan, which includes 5 invoices per month, and you've already created 5 this month. That's most likely why New invoice isn't doing anything.

To send this one today, you can upgrade to Pro. It costs £15 a month or £150 a year and includes unlimited invoices. As the owner, you can upgrade under Settings › Billing.

Another option is to edit an invoice you've already sent, as long as it has no payments recorded. Open it and choose Edit. The client sees the new version on the same link.

[invoices] Create and send an invoice
Go to Invoices › New invoice, pick a client, add line items and a due date, then choose Send. The client receives an email with a link to view and pay the invoice. You can also copy the link and share it yourself.

[invoices] Correct a paid invoice
To correct a paid or part-paid invoice, issue a credit note from More › Issue credit note and then create a new invoice. Credit notes keep the audit trail intact; paid invoices are never changed in place.

[invoices] Edit an invoice after sending
A sent invoice that has no payments can be edited: open it and choose Edit. The client sees the new version on the same link. An invoice with any payment recorded against it is locked and cannot be edited.

[tax] Add VAT to an invoice
Switch on VAT under Settings › Tax and enter your VAT number. New invoices then add VAT at 20% to each taxable line. You can mark a line as exempt when you add it.

[plans] Free plan
The Free plan costs nothing. It includes 5 invoices per month and 1 user. It does not include automatic reminders, bank sync or team members.

[plans] Pro plan
Pro costs £15 per month or £150 per year. It includes unlimited invoices, up to 5 team members, automatic reminders and bank sync.

Automatic reminders are part of the Pro plan. On the Free plan you can still send a reminder by hand from the invoice page with Send reminder, but nothing is sent automatically.
